# OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-06 > Issues: 83 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 12 | Generated: 2026-11-06 06:09 UTC - [OpenClaw](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw) - [NanoBot](https://github​.com/HKUDS/nanobot) - [Hermes Agent](https://github​.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent) - [PicoClaw](https://github​.com/sipeed/picoclaw) - [NanoClaw](https://github​.com/qwibitai/nanoclaw) - [NullClaw](https://github​.com/nullclaw/nullclaw) - [IronClaw](https://github​.com/nearai/ironclaw) - [LobsterAI](https://github​.com/netease-youdao/LobsterAI) - [Moltis](https://github​.com/moltis-org/moltis) - [CoPaw](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/CoPaw) - [ZeptoClaw](https://github​.com/qhkm/zeptoclaw) - [ZeroClaw](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw) --- ## OpenClaw Deep Dive **OpenClaw Project Digest – 2026‑11‑06** *(generated from the latest GitHub activity)* --- ## 1. Today’s Overview * OpenClaw remains **high‑velocity**: 83 issues and 500 pull‑requests saw activity in the last 24 h, with **329 PRs still open** and **171 already merged/closed**. * The community is battling a mix of **critical regressions** (gateway lock‑ups, session‑state corruption) and **steady feature creep** (model‑pin inheritance, active‑memory escalation, UI refinements). * A **new stable release** (v2026.11.1) landed today, focusing on safer macOS configuration handling and more reliable channel replies (Telegram, Discord, webhooks). * Overall health: **high engagement** but **pressure on maintainers** – many high‑priority bugs are still open and a sizable backlog of “no‑new‑fix‑pr” tickets remains. --- ## 2. Releases ### **v2026.11.1** – 2026‑11‑01 * **Safer macOS settings** – failed config saves no longer overwrite stored secrets; turning off Tailscale exposure preserves Gateway authentication. *(Fixes #187600, #187597)* * **More reliable channel replies** – Telegram, Discord, and webhook conversations now expose fewer “partial‑reply” edge‑cases. * **No breaking‑API changes** – release is a drop‑in for existing installations. * **Upgrade notes** – macOS users should restart the app to pick up the corrected settings flow; no database migrations required. [Release notes →](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/releases/tag/v2026.11.1) --- ## 3. Project Progress (PRs) | PR | Area | Size / Risk | Status | Why it matters | |----|------|-------------|--------|----------------| | **#193980** | `openclaw-id` – account‑less node enrollment | XL – high compatibility/security risk | **Open** (awaiting proof) | Lays groundwork for headless nodes to bootstrap without a user account, a prerequisite for future distributed‑agent fleets. | | **#193952** | UI / Models – customizable provider names & artwork | XL – UI impact | **Open** (needs author) | Gives operators branding control; aligns with upcoming “plugin‑catalog” UI refresh. | | **#193984** | Web UI – nested search settings rendering fix | S – low risk | **Open** (waiting on author) | Improves usability of advanced search config pages; a common source of UI complaints. | | **#193945** | Gateway – preserve earlier attachments after an interrupted chat | L – moderate | **Open** (ready for maintainer) | Fixes a regression that caused image/video loss when a turn was resumed, directly addressing user‑reported data‑loss bugs. | | **#193987** | CLI – image‑edit hangs on FIFO input | S – low | **Open** (needs review) | Prevents indefinite hangs for pipelines that stream image data via named pipes. | | **#193982** | Node‑host – OpenClaw‑ID tunnel connectivity | XL – high | **Open** (feature preview) | Extends node‑to‑gateway communication beyond LAN/Tailscale, a key step toward “cloud‑agnostic” deployments. | | **#193990** | `openclaw-id` – delegated‑owner revocation escape fix | M – moderate | **Open** (ready) | Closes a security loophole where a compromised delegated device could survive revocation. | | **#193956** | Markdown – NaN chunk limit silently drops messages | XS – low | **Open** (fixes #193928) | Directly resolves a bug that caused entire outbound messages to disappear on some channels. | | **#193991** | macOS – gateway status UI stuck after gateway exit | S – UI bug | **Open** | Prevents confusing “Using existing gateway” stale status. | *Overall*: **171 PRs were merged/closed** yesterday, showing a healthy throughput. The majority of open PRs are small‑to‑medium UI or integration fixes, while a handful of large‑scale features (node‑enrollment, ID tunnel) are still pending author review or maintainer sign‑off. --- ## 4. Community Hot Topics | Issue / PR | Comments | Category | Key Insight | |------------|----------|----------|--------------| | **#160959** – *Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins* | 75 | Critical regression (P0) | The plugin‑capture pipeline introduced in 2026.9.6 is still causing multi‑minute event‑loop pauses; the community is providing extensive reproduction logs. | | **#177656** – *Native host exec shared‑state integrity‑admission error* | 29 | Runtime failure (P1) | 28+ failures on the latest stable (2026.10.5) suggest a systemic integrity‑check regression after a recent core refactor. | | **#141474** – *Collector child sessions_yield deadlock; outputSchema inert* | 14 | Session‑state bug (P2) | Tied to the upcoming historical‑state recovery work (`v2026.11.5‑beta.1`). Users are awaiting stable integration. | | **#193734** – *Package‑swap refuses updates on npm‑global install* | 2 | Update‑pipeline blocker (P2) | Indicates a lingering permission‑model issue after the 2026.9.8 release; many operators report being “stuck” on that version. | | **#193980** – *Define account‑less node enrollment* | 0 (but high rating) | Feature request (P2) | Early adopters are already building headless agents; this PR is a high‑visibility roadmap item. | | **#193952** – *Custom provider names & artwork* | 0 | UI/UX enhancement (P2) | Operators want branding consistency across multi‑provider setups, a recurring request in the Slack/Discord community. | **Underlying need:** A large proportion of the chatter revolves around **gateway resilience**, **session state integrity**, and **customizability of the UI/agent experience**. The high comment counts reflect both the severity of regressions and the community’s willingness to provide detailed repro steps. --- ## 5. Bugs & Stability (ranked by severity) | Severity | Issue | Summary | Status | Fix PR (if any) | |----------|-------|---------|--------|-----------------| | **Critical (P0)** | **#160959** – Gateway freeze on large plugin capture | Event loop blocked for minutes during plugin generation & model republishes. | **Open** (needs investigation) | None yet | | **High (P1)** | **#177656** – Shared‑state integrity‑admission error in native host exec | 28+ failures on stable 2026.10.5; aborts child processes. | **Open** | None | | **High (P1)** | **#142874** – Session stuck after companion‑app “Reply operation has no active tool authority” | Persistent UI freeze; only full gateway restart recovers. | **Open** | None | | **High (P1)** | **#142813** – Inbound message mid‑turn drops reply & stalls queue (WhatsApp) | Race condition leads to minutes‑long stalls. | **Open** | None | | **High (P1)** | **#193262** – Docker startup fails on Windows bind‑mounted state dir (ENOENT) | Regression since 2026.9.3; prevents Windows‑hosted deployments. | **Open** | None | | **Medium (P2)** | **#182891** – Prompt cache never reused (token loss) | Cache reads drop to 0 each request, costing ~16 M tokens. | **Open** | None | | **Medium (P2)** | **#185656 (closed)** – Large zstd transcript archive exceeds Node string limit (media‑persistence migration) | Still reproduces on 2026.10.5 despite prior fix. | **Closed** (no fix merged) | None | | **Medium (P2)** | **#193928 / #193956** – NaN chunk limit silently drops outbound message | Fixed in PR #193956 (still open for review). | **Open** | #193956 | | **Medium (P2)** | **#193734** – Package‑swap update refusal (npm‑global) | Update process aborts with “unsafe permissions”. | **Open** | None | *Takeaway:* The **gateway‑blocking** bugs dominate the severity list and have **no corresponding fix PRs yet**, indicating an urgent need for maintainer bandwidth. UI‑related regressions (macOS, iOS) are plentiful but generally lower‑risk. --- ## 6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals | Request | Core Idea | Priority (as labelled) | Likelihood in next release | |---------|-----------|------------------------|----------------------------| | **#151980** – *Session model pins inherit agent fallback chain* | Ensure fallback models still work when a session‑level pin is set. | P2 (diamond lobster) | **High** – directly ties to stability of model fallback; likely contested in upcoming beta (v2026.11.5). | | **#151178** – *Active Memory delegate escalation to plugin* | Allow a plugin to decide when to trigger deep recall. | P2 (silver shellfish) | **Medium** – architectural change; may be scheduled after memory‑core indexing work (PR #193815). | | **#151173** – *Memory‑core recall anchor bug* | Fix ambiguous range selection during rehydration. | P2 (diamond lobster) | **Medium‑High** – memory core is a hot area; a fix may land in the next beta. | | **#193952** – *Custom provider names & artwork* | UI branding for multiple providers. | P2 (gold shrimp) | **Medium** – UI work is in progress; could be shipped in the next minor. | | **#193980** – *Account‑less node enrollment* | Headless nodes get a bootstrap identity. | P2 (unranked krab) | **Medium‑High** – strategic for distributed deployments; likely a focus for the next quarter. | | **#184709** – *ElevenLabs batch transcription keyterm prompting* | Extend transcription API with custom vocabularies. | P3 | **Low‑Medium** – niche, may be delayed. | | **#191008** – *ClawHub skill: Company Research Job (paid)* | Monetization of a skill for “search‑tier exhausted” cases. | P3 | **Low** – business‑model experiment, not a core roadmap item. | The **model‑pin fallback** and **memory‑core stability** items appear most aligned with the current bug‑fix thrust and are probable candidates for inclusion in the upcoming **v2026.11.5‑beta** series. --- ## 7. User Feedback Summary * **Gateway reliability** – Users repeatedly report “gateway blocked for minutes” when loading large external plugins or when the state directory is mounted from Windows drives. This is the most urgent pain point. * **Session state & data loss** – Issues such as mid‑turn inbound message drops (WhatsApp, #142813) and lost attachments after interrupted chats (#193945) cause operational disruption for agents handling high‑volume channels. * **UI/UX friction** – macOS Settings sluggishness (#192667), web‑UI search‑settings rendering (#193984), and hidden 1Password button (#193985) are repeatedly flagged, indicating a need for polish in the native desktop clients. * **Configuration & update failures** – The package‑swap update blocker (#193734) and the Docker bind‑mount startup crash (#193262) leave a subset of operators unable to upgrade, driving frustration and “stuck on old version” sentiment. * **Positive signals** – The safer macOS config handling in the new release and the steady stream of PRs addressing UI clarity (warning callouts, repeated lookups) show the team is listening to usability concerns. Overall, **operational stability** (gateway, sessions, update pipeline) is the dominant user‑reported dissatisfaction, while **branding/customization** and **headless‑node capabilities** generate excitement for future development. --- ## 8. Backlog Watch (Stale / High‑Impact Items) | Issue | Age / Stale Tag | Reason for attention | |-------|----------------|-----------------------| | **#127195** – “changed while starting work” error across 16 call sites | Stale (opened Aug 21) | No discriminators; prevents root‑cause debugging; impacts many production agents. | | **#112638** – `session.maintenance` max‑entries overflow | Stale (opened Jul 22) | Could cause uncontrolled disk growth; still open despite being a **beta release blocker**. | | **#124306** – Exec approval card omits mount‑point warning | Stale (opened Aug 15) | Security‑relevant: operators may unintentionally `rm -rf` a mount. | | **#166964** – Subagent completion delivery fails on revoked authority | Stale (opened Oct 8) | Leads to permanent dead‑locked sessions; no fix yet. | | **#193734** – Package‑swap update refusal (npm‑global) | Open (opened Nov 5) | Directly blocks many users from upgrading; needs a quick fix. | | **#193262** – Docker start failure on Windows bind‑mount | Open (Nov 5) | Prevents a whole class of Windows‑based deployments; a regression. | | **#185656** – Large zstd transcript archive overflow (closed but unfixed) | Closed (Nov 6) | Regression persists on stable 2026.10.5 despite prior PR; needs re‑evaluation. | | **#193845** – Litestream WAL warning spam | Open (Nov 6) | Log noise can hide real issues; low‑severity but high‑frequency. | | **#193868** – Exec code‑mode bridge corruption after hours (macOS) | Open (Nov 6) | Affects long‑running macOS gateways; could cause widespread outages. | **Recommendation:** Prioritize the **gateway‑blocking** bugs and the **update‑pipeline** failures (issues #160959, #193734, #193262). Simultaneously, address the **session‑state** edge‑cases that cause dead‑locks (issues #127195, #112638, #166964). These items collectively affect the largest user base and the most critical production workloads. --- *Prepared by the OpenClaw analytics team – 2026‑11‑06.* --- ## Cross-Ecosystem Comparison **Cross‑Project Comparison Report – Personal AI‑Assistant / Agent Ecosystem** *Data snapshot: 2026‑11‑06 (24 h activity window)* --- ### 1. Ecosystem Overview The open‑source personal‑AI‑assistant landscape is maturing from hobby‑level bots to production‑grade orchestration platforms. Most projects now ship **gateway / daemon layers**, **session‑state managers**, and **plugin‑catalogs** that enable third‑party skills. A clear trend is the push toward **head‑less / account‑less node enrollment** and **key‑less service providers** to lower operational friction. Security‑hardening (credential redaction, sandboxed exec) and cross‑platform stability (macOS, Windows, Linux containers) dominate the current engineering focus. --- ### 2. Activity Comparison | Project | Issues (last 24 h) | PRs (last 24 h) | Release in last 24 h? | Health Score* | |--------|-------------------|----------------|----------------------|---------------| | **OpenClaw** | 83 (mix of regressions & feature requests) | 500 (≈ 329 open) | ✅ v2026.11.1 (stable) | **High** (high velocity, but critical bug backlog) | | **NanoBot** | 2 | 18 | – (0.4.1 pending) | **Medium‑High** (steady UI polish, low‑severity bugs) | | **Hermes Agent** | 11 | 50 | ✅ v0.23.0 (yesterday) | **High** (rapid refactor, but several P2‑P1 regressions) | | **PicoClaw** | 1 | 4 (dependabot) | – | **Low‑Medium** (maintenance mode) | | **NanoClaw** | 3 | 16 | – (image‑refresh only) | **High** (security hardening, installer fixes) | | **NullClaw** | 0 | 0 | – | **Low** (dormant) | | **IronClaw** | 0 | 0 | – | **Low** (dormant) | | **LobsterAI** | 1 | 16 | – (no tag) | **High** (desktop‑client stability sprint) | | **Moltis** | 0 | 1 (new provider) | – | **Low‑Medium** (single feature PR) | | **CoPaw** | 14 | 37 | – (no tag) | **High** (burst of bug‑fixes & feature work) | | **ZeroClaw** | 5 | 50 | – (pre‑v0.9.0 sprint) | **High** (large cross‑component PRs) | \*Health Score assesses **signal‑to‑noise** (ratio of critical fixes vs backlog) and **maintenance bandwidth**. “High” = active development with most bugs being addressed; “Low” = little recent activity or only routine housekeeping. --- ### 3. OpenClaw’s Position | Dimension | OpenClaw | Typical Peer | |-----------|----------|---------------| | **Core technical approach** | Monolithic “gateway‑agent” binary + extensive channel adapters (Telegram, Discord, webhooks). Emphasises **session‑state persistence** (SQLite + Litestream) and **model‑pin inheritance**. | Hermes / ZeroClaw split gateway + daemon; CoPaw uses a micro‑service‑style RPC layer; NanoClaw leans on container‑based agents. | | **Community size & velocity** | > 800 issues, > 500 PRs in 24 h → one of the *largest* active contributor bases. | CoPaw (≈ 50 PRs) and ZeroClaw (≈ 50 PRs) are comparable but smaller; NanoBot and LobsterAI have tighter, more UI‑focused core teams. | | **Advantages** | • **Mature plugin catalog** and a well‑documented “openclaw‑id” enrollment framework (even if still pending).
• **Stable release cadence** (monthly patches, no breaking‑API changes).
• **Broad channel coverage** (Telegram, Discord, webhooks) out‑of‑the‑box. | • Projects like Hermes gain a **cleaner separation** of gateway/agent, reducing crash surface.
• CoPaw provides **tight integration** with memory‑core and searchable chats.
• ZeroClaw focuses on **runtime security** (orphaned‑session retirement). | | **Weaknesses relative to peers** | • Heavy **bug backlog** on gateway freeze & session‑state corruption (P0‑P1).
• Large PR queue (329 open) strains maintainer bandwidth.
• UI regressions on macOS/Windows still open. | • Hermes already shipped the **account‑less node enrollment** feature that OpenClaw only plans.
• ZeroClaw’s “orphaned‑session retirement” directly solves a bug OpenClaw still carries. | Overall, OpenClaw is the **de‑facto reference implementation** with the broadest channel ecosystem, but it is **most exposed** to regressions because of that breadth. Projects that have deliberately split responsibilities (Hermes, ZeroClaw) enjoy faster turnaround on critical bugs. --- ### 4. Shared Technical Focus Areas | Need | Projects Raising It | Specific Requirement | |------|----------------------|----------------------| | **Gateway resilience / session‑state integrity** | OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, ZeroClaw, CoPaw | Prevent long‑running event‑loop freezes, ensure graceful cleanup of orphaned RPC sessions, avoid attachment loss on interrupted turns. | | **Key‑less / low‑credential service providers** | NanoClaw (key‑less web search), Moltis (Keenable), LobsterAI (key‑less Parallel search), NanoBot (workspace picker for offline use) | Provide *out‑of‑the‑box* providers that do **not** require API keys, with graceful fallback and rate‑limit handling. | | **UI/UX polish & cross‑platform consistency** | NanoBot, LobsterAI, CoPaw, NanoClaw, OpenClaw (macOS UI bugs) | Consistent layout on high‑DPI displays, reliable copy‑paste of rich media, stable model‑switch timeline entries. | | **Plugin / skill catalog extensibility** | OpenClaw (plugin‑catalog), Hermes (hermes‑mark‑words), CoPaw (skill creator), ZeroClaw (plugin webhook RPC) | Standardised manifest schema, versioned publishing, ability to read rendered assistant text, safe dependency resolution. | | **Security hardening (credential redaction, sandboxed exec)** | LobsterAI (log redaction), NanoClaw (localhost‑only admin API), ZeroClaw (orphaned‑session retirement), OpenClaw (gateway config lock‑ups) | Ensure no secret leaks in logs, restrict external exposure of admin endpoints, enforce least‑privilege for delegated devices. | | **Headless / account‑less node enrollment** | OpenClaw (#193980), Hermes (node‑host tunnel), ZeroClaw (runtime daemon), NanoClaw (Docker install scripts) | Bootstrap nodes without a user account, enable fleet‑scale deployments behind NAT/firewalls. | --- ### 5. Differentiation Analysis | Aspect | OpenClaw | NanoBot | Hermes Agent | PicoClaw | NanoClaw | LobsterAI | Moltis | CoPaw | ZeroClaw | |--------|----------|----------|-------------|----------|----------|-----------|--------|-------|----------| | **Primary Target** | General‑purpose assistant with *maximum* channel coverage. | Web‑UI‑first personal bot, heavy on UI ergonomics. | High‑performance desktop client + plugin ecosystem. | Minimal reference implementation (focus on core gateway). | Security‑hardened container‑based agent for enterprise deployments. | Consumer‑grade desktop client (focused on Chinese market). | Lightweight web‑search abstraction layer. | Full‑stack collaborative chat & memory engine. | Enterprise‑grade gateway split with strong runtime security. | | **Architecture** | Monolithic gateway + embedded SQLite. | Single‑process web UI + TypeScript front‑end. | Separate **gateway daemon** + **desktop UI** (Electron). | Simple Go binary (no UI). | Docker‑based multi‑container stack (gateway + DB). | Electron + OpenClaw core (desktop). | Go library + plugin API. | Micro‑service‑style RPC + memory core + channel adapters. | Core daemon + RPC‑based plugin & dashboard layer. | | **Key Feature Emphasis** | **Channel adapters**, “openclaw‑id” enrollment, model‑pin fallback. | UI placeholders, live context graph, type‑safe CLI. | **Node‑host tunnel**, offline skill distillation (Trace2Skill). | Basic gateway start/stop. | **Credential isolation**, hardened installer, multi‑platform CI. | **Auto‑compaction**, inline‑image copy‑paste, login‑benefit UI. | **Key‑less search** (Keenable). | **Search & Agentic conversation**, plugin‑page navigation, memory tagging. | **Orphaned‑session retirement**, scoped dashboard RPC, multi‑model provider registry. | | **User‑base** | Broad (individuals, SMEs, early‑adopters). | UI‑centric developers, Windows‑heavy users. | Power users who need **desktop control & extensibility**. | Minimal, experimental developers. | Enterprises needing **secure, container‑first** deployments. | Chinese‑market consumers, heavy desktop users. | Developers needing **plug‑and‑play web‑search**. | Teams requiring **collaborative chat & searchable memory**. | Organizations building **multi‑tenant AI gateways**. | --- ### 6. Community Momentum & Maturity | Tier | Projects | Rationale | |------|----------|-----------| | **Rapid‑iteration (high PR/issue churn, frequent merges)** | OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, CoPaw, ZeroClaw | > 40 PRs per day, active bug‑fix sprint, upcoming minor releases. | | **Stabilizing / Feature‑polish** | NanoBot, LobsterAI, NanoClaw | PR volume moderate; most merged items are UI/installer hardening rather than core redesign. | | **Maintenance / Low activity** | PicoClaw, Moltis, NullClaw, IronClaw | Only dependency updates or a single feature PR; no releases, limited community. | | **Emerging** | Moltis, PicoClaw | New feature (key‑less provider) but small contributor pool; opportunity for growth. | --- ### 7. Trend Signals 1. **Headless federation** – Multiple repos (OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw, NanoClaw) are prioritising *account‑less node enrollment* and tunnel‑based communication, indicating that operators want to spin up large fleets without per‑node credentials. 2. **Key‑less service access** – The rise of “no‑API‑key” search providers (NanoClaw, Moltis, LobsterAI) and UI toggles for offline models reflects a market pressure to reduce external credential management and avoid rate‑limit throttling. 3. **Self‑learning skill pipelines** – Requests such as NanoClaw’s “record task solution → reusable skill” and CoPaw’s “keyword/agentic conversation search” show a clear desire for agents that **capture** and **re‑use** execution traces, moving toward autonomous skill generation. 4. **Security & privacy hardening** – Redaction of OAuth tokens (LobsterAI), localhost‑only admin APIs (NanoClaw), and orphaned‑session cleanup (ZeroClaw) are now standard checklist items, underscoring enterprise‑level compliance expectations. 5. **Cross‑platform UI consistency** – Repeated UI regressions on macOS/Windows (OpenClaw, LobsterAI, NanoBot) and the push for adaptive placeholders, copy‑paste fidelity, and model‑switch timeline entries signal that developers view the **desktop client** as a primary user‑facing product, not just a debugging console. 6. **Plugin‑first extensibility** – A growing set of PRs adds **plugin‑catalog** features, webhook RPC dispatch, and standardized manifest schemas, implying the ecosystem is converging on a *marketplace* model where third‑party skills can be discovered, installed, and sandboxed automatically. --- **Implications for AI‑Agent Developers** - Choose a **gateway‑centric** stack (OpenClaw, Hermes, ZeroClaw) if you need **wide channel coverage** and are prepared to handle gateway‑level bugs. - Opt for **headless‑node** capable platforms when scaling fleets (Hermes, ZeroClaw) or when operating in restricted environments. - If **desktop UI polish** and **language‑specific ergonomics** are critical (e.g., Chinese market), LobsterAI or NanoBot provide the most refined front‑ends. - For **security‑first deployments** (enterprise), NanoClaw’s hardened installer and ZeroClaw’s session retirement give a strong baseline. - Projects that emphasize **skill‑learning** (CoPaw, NanoClaw) are best suited for teams building autonomous, self‑optimising agents. *Prepared by the Open‑Source AI‑Agent Analyst (2026‑11‑06).* --- ## Peer Project Reports

Overall the project appears stable, with a strong focus on UI polish, performance optimisation, and bug‑release hygiene. --- ### 2.
